newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Kim urges real-name system be left alone.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Kim urges real-name system be left alone.

text.p: South Korean President Kim Young-sam said that the basic principle behind a real-name financial transaction system should be left alone, a presidential spokesman said on Tuesday.
"Any revision should not damage the basic principle of the real-name system," Kim was quoted by the spokesman as telling new finance minister Kang Kyong-shik in a meeting on Monday.
When Kang was appointed new minister earlier this month, he told reporters he would review the real-name system, introduced to end dubious financial deals.
The system bans the use of false names in all financial transactions and is widely thought to have caused bottlenecks in the economy.
Kang's remarks fanned speculation that the government would allow false-name trading in long-term bonds to flush underground money into the economy.
Hopes that a planned new government economic package for Thursday would involve a revision of the real-name system boosted the Seoul stock market on Saturday and Monday.

"Supplementary measures to revise the real-name system should be sought through a thorough public examination," Kim said. The system is one of Kim's salvoes in a war against corruption and tax evasion which has brought down many senior politicians, bureaucrats and military leaders.
